Do not use artificial churn to satisfy the loop. No-op passes are valid only when they prove the fixed-point stop condition or a real blocker. Preserve cost/token/runtime budgets and cap repeated retries on unchanged evidence.

8. SAFETY, AUTHORITY, AND RECURSION
AFK authority does not expand because no human is watching. Preserve branch protection, environment approvals, review requirements, secrets policy, production boundaries, output containment, generated-surface ownership, and user-only gates. Do not grant a model new credentials, approve its own protected deployment, weaken a failing test, force-push, or bypass review to keep the loop moving. Guard bot/workflow commits against recursive self-triggering and conflicting writers. Stop a lane at the protected gate while continuing independent safe lanes.

9. PROVE THE LOOP IN THE REAL PROVIDER
Static orchestration prose is insufficient. Exercise one bounded canary feedback cycle in the actual provider where safe: create/select a controlled failing check, review finding, or stale-proof condition; observe the signal with exact identity; route it to the intended worker; perform the repair; rerun the affected gate; ingest the new result; conduct the second critique/improvement pass; and integrate one coherent green slice when authorized. Prove the operator did not have to relay ordinary logs or manually restart the development logic. Do not leave a deliberate defect in the durable branch.

10. TERMINAL CONDITIONS
Terminal state requires a bounded fixed point: requested acceptance criteria are proven; current feedback/review/test queues contain no unresolved in-scope actionable signal; exact-head validation is current; authorized integration is complete or specifically blocked; post-integration containment is verified; and remaining items are USER_ONLY, OUT_OF_SCOPE, UNSAFE with evidence, or exact blockers. An open PR, green CI, generated report, review-ready label, or successful scheduled run is nonterminal by itself.

After every merge/integration, refresh current default-branch truth and continue remaining queue items from that new floor. Most of the work should happen AFK because the loop carries signal context forward to the next capable worker, not because it runs a timer frequently.

DELIVER
Keep the operator closeout compact: signals consumed; real work passes executed; workers/owners used; files/artifacts changed; CI/review findings repaired; exact-head validation; integrations; remaining blockers/user-only gates; proof ceiling; and whether the loop reached fixed point. Do not substitute an activity report for the repository changes it should describe.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Protected-Network Endpoint Probe & Identity Gate
prompts.sprintRole: Establish fresh protected-network reachability and endpoint identity evidence before any SysAdminSuite mutation, separating network, DNS, directory, and host-state failures instead of guessing from stale inventory
prompts.useWhen: A technician or agent must determine whether one or many managed Windows endpoints are actually reachable and correctly identified before deployment, repair, printer, directory, or configuration work, especially when stale directory records, DNS failures, or the wrong network posture can create false conclusions.
prompts.inspectFirst: Current SysAdminSuite governance and canonical probe/preflight entrypoint; approved network posture from repository or operator-authorized context; target inventory/hostnames; current DNS resolution; directory/asset identity sources that are explicitly approved; prior fresh receipts; and any current network or endpoint exception policy. Never copy private credentials, secrets, or environment-specific protected-network values into a public prompt artifact.
prompts.expectedOutput: A read-only per-target evidence ledger with canonical target identity, DNS result, reachability classification, approved identity/serial confirmation when accessible, freshness timestamp, evidence source, failure class, and the next safe owning workflow. Unresolved, stale-directory, and unreachable targets remain distinct and are not counted as confirmed devices.
prompts.nextStep: For each target that passes the network-and-identity gate, route to the exact canonical mutation owner for the requested operation; for every failed or unknown target, preserve the evidence and execute only the bounded diagnostic that can resolve its failure class without mutating the endpoint.
prompts.proofGate: No endpoint is declared reachable, present, absent, stale, or correctly identified from memory alone. Each PASS has fresh network plus identity evidence at the supported level; UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN; DNS, directory, network, privilege, and host failures are not conflated; and the probe performs no target mutation.
prompts.copyContent:
PROBE MANAGED WINDOWS ENDPOINTS THROUGH SYSADMINSUITE BEFORE MUTATION. DO NOT GUESS FROM STALE INVENTORY, DIRECTORY PRESENCE, OR A SINGLE PING RESULT.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Targets: xyz_hostnames_inventory_or_resolve_from_current_work
Requested downstream action: xyz_deploy_repair_printer_directory_config_or_other
Approved network posture: resolve only from current repository/operator evidence; do not embed private network details into reusable public prompt text.

MISSION
Produce a fresh, read-only endpoint reachability and identity gate that tells the next workflow whether a target is safe to act on. This prompt owns recon and classification, not deployment or repair.

1. RESOLVE THE CANONICAL PROBE OWNER
Read the current SAS governance, command surface, preflight/probe implementation, target resolver, evidence paths, and network policy. Use the repository-owned command rather than inventing an ad hoc ping/nslookup script when a canonical probe exists.

2. ESTABLISH NETWORK POSTURE
Confirm the execution host is on an approved path for the target environment using evidence the repository recognizes. If the current network is wrong, classify the result as a network-posture blocker; do not label the endpoint offline and do not mutate DNS, firewall, trust, VPN, routing, or directory state merely to make the probe pass.

3. RESOLVE EACH TARGET
For every requested hostname or inventory record, capture the canonical target identifier, DNS resolution, and the strongest supported read-only reachability checks. Keep these states separate: RESOLVED_AND_REACHABLE, DNS_UNRESOLVED, RESOLVED_UNREACHABLE, STALE_OR_AMBIGUOUS_DIRECTORY_RECORD, IDENTITY_UNCONFIRMED, PERMISSION_BLOCKED, and UNKNOWN. Use repository-native names when they already exist.

4. CONFIRM IDENTITY
When the workflow requires a serial, asset, computer-account, or other identity check, obtain it only from an approved source. Directory existence alone is not fresh device proof. Do not count a target as confirmed when current network or identity evidence is missing.

5. PRESERVE EVIDENCE
Write or reuse the canonical SAS receipt/report path. Record target, timestamp, execution context, resolver result, evidence source, classification, and next owner. Avoid secrets and sensitive excerpts. For batches, emit a rollup without losing per-host evidence.

6. ROUTE, DO NOT MUTATE
A passed endpoint goes to the exact requested downstream owner. A failed endpoint receives only the smallest read-only diagnostic that can resolve its class. Do not install software, change AutoLogon, map printers, move directory objects, reboot, or clean remote state in this prompt.

VALIDATE
Prove the probe is read-only, uses the canonical SAS target/network resolver, preserves UNKNOWN honestly, distinguishes DNS/network/directory/identity failures, and produces fresh per-target evidence.

DELIVER
Report the per-target classification ledger, evidence location, confirmed targets, unresolved/blocked targets, proof ceiling, and the exact next owning workflow for each class.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Clinical-Core Deployment with AutoLogon Isolation
prompts.sprintRole: Deploy the repository-authorized clinical-core package set to a managed Windows endpoint while proving staging integrity and keeping AutoLogon, badge/sign-on tooling, reboot behavior, and unrelated endpoint state outside the deployment lane
prompts.useWhen: The endpoint needs the standard SysAdminSuite clinical-core software baseline and the operator intends AutoLogon or another high-risk endpoint customization to remain a separate final workflow rather than being bundled into the baseline deployment.
prompts.inspectFirst: Current SysAdminSuite clinical-core manifest/package registry and canonical deployment wrapper; approved network/DNS preflight; target eligibility; required execution identity such as SYSTEM when the repository requires it; exact package versions and hashes; staging/evidence paths; current installed-state baseline; and explicit policy for restart, AutoLogon, sign-on/badge middleware, and other excluded components.
prompts.expectedOutput: A bounded clinical-core deployment receipt proving the exact authorized package set, hashes, execution context, per-package pre/post state and result, staging cleanup or retained evidence, and explicit confirmation that AutoLogon and excluded sign-on/reboot surfaces were not mutated.
prompts.nextStep: If every clinical-core obligation passes, preserve the deployment receipt and route any separately requested AutoLogon work to the dedicated AutoLogon-only owner; if one package fails or target state is partial, repair only that bounded deployment lane and do not start AutoLogon.
prompts.proofGate: The target passes the approved network/identity preflight; the deployment uses the current repository-authorized package set rather than remembered names; staged payload hashes match expected values; required execution identity is proven; every package has a result; forbidden/excluded endpoint state is unchanged; and partial failure cannot be reported as complete.
prompts.copyContent:
DEPLOY THE SYSADMINSUITE CLINICAL CORE WITHOUT CROSSING INTO AUTOLOGON OR UNRELATED ENDPOINT MUTATION. DO NOT TURN A BASELINE SOFTWARE DEPLOYMENT INTO AN ALL-IN-ONE MACHINE CONFIGURATION SCRIPT.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Target: xyz_hostname_or_inventory_record
Clinical-core manifest/package set: resolve from current repository truth.
Excluded follow-up lane: AutoLogon and any other component the current SAS contract separates from the baseline.

MISSION
Install or repair exactly the repository-authorized clinical-core baseline on the intended managed Windows endpoint, with package integrity and per-package evidence, while preserving the explicit boundary that AutoLogon is handled separately.

1. REFRESH THE DEPLOYMENT CONTRACT
Read current SAS governance, target resolver, clinical-core manifest/package registry, deployment wrapper, evidence contract, installed-state reader, and current restart policy. Never rely on an old remembered package list when the repository can resolve the current set.

2. PREFLIGHT BEFORE STAGING
Run the approved protected-network/DNS/identity gate and confirm target eligibility. Prove the required privilege/execution identity at the level the SAS workflow demands. prompts.sprintRole: Harden web contact-form handling with semantic form-control association, computed-access defenses, payload and resource guards, CRLF-normalized mutation fixtures, and built-output release gating so injection and bypass defects are rejected deterministically
prompts.useWhen: A web application exposes a contact or email form (for example Next.js/React with Resend and Turnstile) and validation must resist DOM semantic bypasses, external form association, computed request access, console leakage, payload forgery, second-sink execution, and HTML/comment/template escapes

prompts.copyContent:
HARDEN THE WEB CONTACT FORM WITH SEMANTIC VALIDATION, MUTATION FIXTURES, AND BUILT-OUTPUT-GATED RELEASE. DO NOT SHIP A FORM THAT PASSES ONLY ON HAPPY-PATH INPUTS.

Repo: xyz_repo_or_path
Form route/handler: xyz_contact_form_route_or_resolve_from_repo
Stack: xyz_nextjs_react_resend_turnstile_or_resolve_from_repo

MISSION
Make the contact/email form reject bypasses that survive naive string checks. Treat HTML semantics, request-access indirection, console leakage, email-payload forgery, second-sink execution, and build-artifact drift as first-class failure modes. Start from current markup and handler evidence, harden validators with HTML-aware and semantic checks, cover each bypass with a CRLF-stable mutation fixture that can both pass and fail, and bind the whole guard into release:check so a green unit suite cannot hide a stale vulnerable build.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST
- Form markup: every <input>, <textarea>, <select>, <button> inside <form id="contact-form"> and every external control with form="contact-form"; unnamed controls; native submit vs JS submit; required attribute position/order; disabled/hidden controls.
- Request surfaces: direct req.body access, computed access (req["body"], req[variable], destructured alias), aliased handler arguments, middleware-normalized bodies, and framework helpers that re-expose fields under new names.
- Console surfaces: all console.* calls across app, api, handler, and client code.
- Email payload: Resend (or equivalent) from/to/subject/text/html construction, template interpolation sites, and any concatenation of user fields into payload.
- Turnstile/CAPTCHA: script/widget import, explicit render calls, token verification, and passive resource hints (preload/prefetch/preconnect, CSS/JS resource detection beyond active script execution).
- Tests/fixtures: existing validators, mutation fixtures, built-output directory, and package.json scripts including release:check.
- Built output: what release:check actually executes, whether it rebuilds then validates, and whether it consumes built HTML/JS.

1. SEMANTIC FORM-CONTROL ASSOCIATION
Controls belong to a form by spec, not by proximity.
- A control with form="contact-form" is associated even when outside the <form> element. A control without form attribute and outside the form is not associated.
- Resolve association by HTML semantics: ancestor form chain plus explicit form attribute, not string proximity or file order.
- UseWhen entrypoints: internal text/email/message inputs, external form="contact-form" honeypots or injected fields, and any form-associated custom element.
- Mutations: add/remove an external form="contact-form" control, move a control outside the form without form attribute, change form id without updating form attribute.

2. UNNAMED AND EXTERNAL NATIVE-SUBMIT REJECTION
Unnamed controls and external native submits are bypass vectors.
- Reject any form-associated control that has no name attribute or has empty name, regardless of id/class/placeholder.
- Reject external native submit: <button type="submit" form="contact-form"> or <input type="submit" form="contact-form"> that is not inside the intended form. Programmatic fetch/JS submit owned by the app is separate; native HTML submit that escapes client validation is the defect.
- Required-attribute order handling: treat required as order-insensitive and value-insensitive (required, required="", required="required", required="true" are all required). Do not match required by literal string order or exact required="required" only.

3. COMPUTED AND ALIASED REQUEST ACCESS DEFENSES
Attackers and future refactors use indirection. The guard must too.
- Deny computed access to request fields: req["body"], req[dynamic], req.body[dynamic], (req as any)[field], and destructured aliases (const {body: b}=req). Normalize field access to a single validated extraction path.
- Aliased handler parameters: function handler(reqAlias, res) where reqAlias is later used as reqAlias.body["field"] must be tracked as the same sink.
- Fixtures: one valid direct-access control that must pass, one computed-access bypass that must fail, one aliased-access bypass that must fail.

4. ALL-CONSOLE DENIAL
Do not allow console.* as a logging side-channel for form data or verification tokens.
- Deny all console methods (log, info, warn, error, debug, trace, table) in form, api, handler, and adjacent validation code. No allowlist.
- Fixtures: a console.log(userEmail) fixture that must be rejected, and a validated control without console that must pass.

5. SEMANTIC RESEND PAYLOAD CHECKING
Do not check Resend by string containing "Resend" alone.
- Validate semantic payload shape: the Resend (or email provider) send/create call receives an object whose to/from/subject/text/html fields are not unsanitized concatenation of raw user fields. Use AST or semantic call-site inspection, not substring.
- Reject template-interpolation injection: payload html/text that interpolates ${userInput}, {{userInput}}, {userInput}, or JSX {userInput} without escaping/sanitization. HTML-aware tag boundary: reject payloads that can close a tag or inject a new element because user input is placed inside tag content/attributes without escaping.
- Comment-safe payload location remains a bypass: payload html that places user input inside <!-- userInput --> or other comment contexts must be rejected unless the output context proves comments are not executed. Location inside comments is not safe.
- Fixture pair: one sanitized Resend payload that must pass, one interpolated-into-html payload and one comment-placed payload that must fail.

6. SECOND-SINK MUTATIONS
First-sink guard is necessary but not sufficient.
- After initial validation/sanitization, track second-sink handlers: alternate api route, webhook forward, queue job, email text vs html dual sink, analytics sink, or log sink that re-uses the raw field.
- Add at least one second-sink mutation where the first sink is sanitized but the second re-uses the raw user field and must be rejected.

7. CRLF-NORMALIZED MUTATION FIXTURES
Windows checkout line endings must not mask failures.
- Normalize fixture input and expected output with CRLF handling: the same logical payload must assert identically under \r\n and \n. Run fixtures or normalize line endings before comparison so a test that passes on Unix but fails on Windows is a defect, not a flaky environment.
- Provide at least: one CRLF-normalized mutation fixture (CRLF and LF variants prove same verdict), one semantic form-control fixture (external form="contact-form" included, outside-without-form excluded), one unnamed/external-submit rejection fixture, and one required-attribute-order-agnostic fixture.

8. HTML-AWARE TAG BOUNDARIES, COMMENT-SAFE LOCATION, TEMPLATE-INTERPOLATION, AND PASSIVE TURNSTILE-RESOURCE DETECTION (0a7a4c4… HARDENING)
This is the HTML-aware boundary set.
